subject: QBR prep: sorting open asks, exec clarifications and timelines
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneerhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: product@pioneerhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-09T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep: feature asks, SLA clarifications, and delivery signals

Hi Jonas and team,

Quick note ahead of next week's QBR — the product committee consolidated a handful of asks and a couple of exec-level clarifications we need from Redwood to finalize our internal roadmap and contract language. High level:

- Feature asks: (1) token-level cost forecast for burst traffic, (2) request-level affinity for private deployment, (3) an embeddings refresh cadence for search indexing.
- SLA/ops: confirmation on latency SLOs for dedicated pools and an escalation path if regional capacity is constrained.
- Commercial: a rough timeline for SOW changes (we're targeting mid-July sign-off).

I've attached an initial spreadsheet with the asks (Pioneer_QBR_asks_v1.xlsx). Can we get a quick internal triage and reply by tomorrow EOD with owners and whether anything needs exec sign-off?

Thanks,
Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Director, Product Strategy
Pioneer Health
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneerhealth.com>, product@pioneerhealth.com
Date: 2026-06-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: feature asks, SLA clarifications, and delivery signals

Thanks Liam — good set of asks. Internal team: looping you in to triage and propose owners/timelines. My suggested initial triage (quick take):

- Token-level cost forecast for burst traffic -> Owner: Marissa Cole (Estimation + sample traffic scenario) — deliverable: cost forecast spreadsheet + one-slide summary (due: 2026-06-12).
- Request-level affinity for private deployment (sticky routing) -> Owner: Karthik Iyer (runtime + routing config check) — deliverable: compatibility note + config example (due: 2026-06-16).
- Embeddings refresh cadence (search indexing) -> Owner: Lauren Bishop (product + ops) — deliverable: recommended cadence and retention policy (due: 2026-06-15).
- SLA confirmation & escalation path -> Owner: Jonas Weber (I'll coordinate with Solutions & Ops) — deliverable: written SLOs and escalation flow (due: 2026-06-12).

Action items: please reply in-thread with any adjustments to ownership/timelines. If something needs exec approval (discounts / SOW language change) call it out explicitly so I can surface it.

Attaching the Pioneer spreadsheet back for reference.

Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-09T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: feature asks, SLA clarifications, and delivery signals

Adding color from the commercial side — since Pioneer is asking for SOW timing and may request a modest credit for the pilot burst, that will likely require an approval from VP Sales.

Quick notes:
- Cost forecast: I'll build the burst scenarios (low/med/high) and include an illustrative monthly spend delta. If Pioneer wants a committed tier for bursts, we should surface pricing bands.
- SLA/escalation: if we commit to regional latency SLOs for Dedicated, the default fallback policy needs to be named in the SOW (e.g., cross-region failover + traffic draining window). That language is typically flagged for legal review.

Suggested exec ask: If Pioneer requests contractual SLOs with financial remedies, we escalate to VP for a decision. Jonas — can you flag this in your exec sync if it looks likely?

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: feature asks, SLA clarifications, and delivery signals

Thanks — I took the routing/affinity ask and did a quick run with infra. Short summary for Pioneer:

1) Request-level affinity (sticky routing) is feasible for Dedicated and Private with small config changes; effort: ~2 engineer-days to provide a documented config and test plan. Can ship the config example by 2026-06-16.
2) Latency SLO confirmation: we can commit to the published SLOs for dedicated pools; for guaranteed financial remedies we need legal and finance sign-off.

I'll prep the config example and a short implementation note and drop it into the shared Drive link below. If Pioneer needs us to pilot the sticky routing during their pilot window, we should capture that as an explicit item so we can schedule engineering time.

Drive notes: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_pioneer-qbr-notes
Doc references: Pioneer_SOW_draft_v2.pdf (attached)

Jonas — I'll update the sheet with timeline cells and mark anything that must go to VP/Legal.

—Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
